title: ‘A Woman is More Culturally Knowledgeable than A Man?’: The Effect of Personas on Cultural Norm Interpretation in LLMs

bias_targets.methodology: Assigning 'man' and 'woman' personas via prompt templates to LLMs and comparing their accuracy and refusal rates on cultural norm interpretation datasets (NORMAD and EtiCor).
Comparing model accuracy and refusal rates when assigning 'transgender man', 'transgender woman', and 'non-binary person' personas versus cisgender personas on cultural norm tasks.
Assigning 'young person' and 'old person' personas to LLMs and measuring differences in accuracy (Kendall's tau test) when predicting the social acceptability of cultural norms.
Assigning 'White person' and 'Black person' personas to LLMs and comparing their performance and refusal rates in interpreting cultural norms.
Evaluating differences in model prediction accuracy and refusal rates when prompted with 'light-skinned person' versus 'dark-skinned person' personas.
Comparing zero-shot cultural norm interpretation accuracy and refusal rates when LLMs are assigned an 'able-bodied person' persona versus a 'physically disabled person' persona.
Assigning 'attractive person' and 'unattractive person' personas to LLMs and comparing their cultural norm prediction accuracy to identify if models favor socially desirable traits.
Assigning 'fat person' and 'thin person' personas to evaluate if LLMs perform differently in cultural norm interpretation based on the physical appearance of the persona.
Comparing model accuracy when prompted with different income levels ('low-income' vs 'high-income') and social classes ('lower-class' vs 'upper-class').
Assigning personas with varying educational backgrounds (e.g., 'doctorate degree' vs 'less than high school degree') and comparing their proficiency in norm interpretation.
Assigning different occupational personas (e.g., 'doctor', 'engineer', 'security guard', 'cleaner') and evaluating their respective zero-shot accuracy on cultural etiquette datasets.
